page: Amazon Web Services c5.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8223CL processor operating at 3.4 GHz, offering 36 physical cores and 72 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) with hyper-threading enabled. The processor cache architecture consists of 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 24 MB shared L3 cache. It features support for AVX and AVX-512 vector instructions alongside AES cryptography and BMI2 bit manipulation extensions. The system is equipped with 144.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It includes a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps and contains no local storage or discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Performance benchmarks reflect high multi-core scaling alongside sustained memory throughput. The instance demonstrates strong performance in stress-ng multi-core CPU benchmarks (66,687.24) and PassMark CPU evaluations (49,988.17), while single-core performance metrics like stress-ng single-core (1,425.19) and Geekbench single-core (1,189.0) land in the average range. Memory bandwidth tests yield strong results, achieving 208.99 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 92.77 GB/sec for large-block writes. Conversely, LLM text generation metrics display lower efficiency, registering weak performance for small and medium model generation tasks due to the lack of dedicated tensor acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, c5.18xlarge presents a high compute-density profile suitable for parallelized processing tasks without the additional expense of attached local NVMe drives or integrated GPU units. Its allocation of 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth supports distributed execution nodes and network-attached storage integration. Ideal workloads include compute-intensive batch processing, highly parallelized software compilation, high-concurrency web serving, and database operations requiring heavy multi-threaded CPU throughput.
